transcript.text: Good morning, everyone. Let's get started on the courtyard set review. We have two options on the table — a masonry courtyard or a modular painted-timber courtyard — and we need to settle on a construction plan that fits within our $180,000 budget so fabrication can begin after this review. Before I make my final approval decision, I'd like to hear from each of you: structural, permit, stunt, and insurance. Please give me your reports and any concerns about either option.
transcript.speaker: A1

transcript.text: I need to flag a critical structural issue from my load test yesterday. The masonry courtyard option would exceed Soundstage 3's 600 kilograms-per-square-meter floor limit, so that option is not viable from a structural standpoint. The modular painted-timber design does pass — but only if we install a 30-millimeter load-spreading deck. My written report is still in the engineering queue, so I'm sharing this verbally now to make sure it's on the record before any approval decision.
transcript.speaker: A2

transcript.text: I need to share a critical heritage-permit issue. I confirmed with the local heritage-permit office this morning that the approved facade may be no wider than exactly 8 meters, and on-stage masonry cutting is prohibited. The permit clerk's email has not yet been added to the production file, so I'm putting this on the record now.
transcript.speaker: A3

transcript.text: I need to flag a critical stunt requirement before any approval decision. My rehearsal assessment found that the scripted horse dismount requires an unobstructed lane exactly 10 meters long and 4 meters wide, with a 2-meter crash mat at its landing end. The choreography note is still awaiting the next stunt meeting, so I'm putting this on the record now to ensure the courtyard set design accommodates this lane.
transcript.speaker: A4

transcript.text: I need to flag a critical insurance coverage issue before any approval decision. I confirmed with the insurer's underwriter that our coverage excludes an open-flame brazier on this stage. However, an LED-flame prop is permitted under the policy if it remains at least 12 meters from the sprinkler-head cluster and its certification is filed before filming. The endorsement for this is currently awaiting countersignature, so I'm putting this on the record now to ensure the courtyard set design accounts for these insurance constraints.
